title: Presheaf differential relations and their sheafified cokernel
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], small in the universe of its presheaf values, and let $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings. A presheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules means a presheaf of abelian groups with a $\mathcal B(U)$-module structure on each value and semilinear restriction maps. For a presheaf of sets $T$, define the free module presheaf $\mathcal B[T](U)=\bigoplus_{t\in T(U)}\mathcal B(U)[t]$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with restrictions $b[t]\mapsto b|_V[t|_V]$. Put
$$F=\mathcal B[\mathcal B],\qquad E=\mathcal B[\mathcal B\times\mathcal B]\oplus\mathcal B[\mathcal B\times\mathcal B]\oplus\mathcal B[\mathcal A].$$
The sectionwise linear maps with generator values
$$r_1[(a,b)]=[a+b]-[a]-[b],\quad r_2[(f,g)]=[fg]-g[f]-f[g],\quad r_3[h]=[\varphi(h)]$$
form a morphism $r:E\to F$ of module presheaves. Let $P(U)=\Omega_{\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal A(U)}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], with restrictions characterized by $d_Ub\mapsto d_V(b|_V)$. These restrictions make $P$ a module presheaf, and the maps $p_U:F(U)\to P(U)$, $[b]\mapsto d_Ub$, form a morphism $p:F\to P$ which is the cokernel of $r$, computed sectionwise. For every module presheaf $M$, its abelian sheafification $M^\#$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] has the canonical $\mathcal B^\#$-module structure extending the original action. In the category of $\mathcal B^\#$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $p^\#:F^\#\to P^\#$ is a cokernel of $r^\#:E^\#\to F^\#$, and for every $U$ and $b\in\mathcal B(U)$ it satisfies
$$p^\#_U(\eta_F([b]))=\eta_P(d_Ub),$$
where $\eta_M:M\to M^\#$ denotes the sheafification unit.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify, proof: the displayed presheaf relation map, its sectionwise differential cokernel, and the final exact-sheafification sentence.

proof.text: For an arrow $v:V\to U$, extend $b[t]\mapsto b|_V[t|_V]$ additively on finite sums. The basis description in [def-weil-pbc-free-module] makes this a semilinear map; identity and composite restrictions agree on every $b[t]$, hence on every sum. This constructs the free module presheaves in the statement. Restricting the three relation generators gives respectively $[a|_V+b|_V]-[a|_V]-[b|_V]$, $[f|_Vg|_V]-g|_V[f|_V]-f|_V[g|_V]$, and $[\varphi_V(h|_V)]$. These are exactly $r_V$ of the restricted generators, since ring restrictions preserve sums and products and $\varphi$ is natural. Thus $r$ is a morphism.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify, proof: presheaf relation map and its sectionwise cokernel

proof.text: For $v:V\to U$, regard $P(V)$ as a $\mathcal B(U)$-module through restriction. The map $b\mapsto d_V(b|_V)$ is a $\mathcal A(U)$-derivation: additivity and Leibniz hold in $P(V)$, and $d_V(\varphi_U(h)|_V)=d_V(\varphi_V(h|_V))=0$. The universal property of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] therefore gives a unique semilinear restriction $P(U)\to P(V)$ carrying $d_Ub$ to $d_V(b|_V)$. Identity and composite restrictions have that same value on every $d_Ub$, so uniqueness proves the presheaf laws. Also $p_V([b|_V])=d_V(b|_V)=p_U([b])|_V$; linearity on the free generators proves that $p$ is natural.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify, proof: presheaf relation map and its sectionwise cokernel

proof.text: At each U, a linear map g from the free symbol module killing r_U defines the function b ↦ g([b]). Evaluating g r_U = 0 on the three kinds of free generators gives additivity, Leibniz and vanishing on the image of A(U). Thus it is a derivation relative to φ_U. The universal property of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] gives a unique linear map from Ω_{B(U)/A(U)} to the target, whose composite with p_U agrees with g on each free generator and hence everywhere. Uniqueness follows because differential generators determine a map from Ω. This proves the sectionwise cokernel property without identifying a separate relation span. The joint reflection of colimits by evaluation in [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-modules-colimits-sectionwise] then proves the presheaf cokernel property.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify, proof: presheaf relation map and its sectionwise cokernel

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] with $\mathcal O=\mathcal B$. It equips the abelian sheafification of every module presheaf $M$ with the canonical compatible $\mathcal B^\#$-module action and gives functorial $\mathcal B^\#$-linear sheafifications $r^\#$ and $p^\#$. Its factorization property states that precomposition with $\eta_M$ is a bijection from module-sheaf maps $M^\#\to N$ to module-presheaf maps $M\to N$, where scalars on $N$ are restricted along $\mathcal B\to\mathcal B^\#$.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules and following adjunction formula

proof.text: The adjunction of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] makes associatedModules a left adjoint. Hence it preserves zero morphisms and colimits, in particular the cokernel cofork from step 3. Applying the standard mapped-cokernel-cofork construction therefore gives the cokernel universal property of p^# for r^#, including r^# ≫ p^# = 0. This is the categorical form of descending a map through the presheaf cokernel and then uniquely extending it across the sheafification unit.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify, proof: presheaf relation map and its sectionwise cokernel

proof.text: The morphism $p^\#$ is characterized by $p^\#\eta_F=\eta_Pp$, by the functorial factorization in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. Evaluating at $U$ on $[b]$ and using $p_U([b])=d_Ub$ from step 3 gives $p^\#_U(\eta_F([b]))=\eta_P(d_Ub)$, as required.

lean.statement: theorem differential_presheaf_relation_cokernel {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {A B : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{max u v}} (φ : A ⟶ B) : ∃ (r : relations A B ⟶ symbols B) (p : symbols B ⟶ relativeDifferentials' φ), (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a b : B.obj U), r.app U (ModuleCat.freeMk (Sum.inl (a, b))) = ModuleCat.freeMk (a + b) - ModuleCat.freeMk a - ModuleCat.freeMk b) ∧ (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (f g : B.obj U), r.app U (ModuleCat.freeMk (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (f, g)))) = ModuleCat.freeMk (f * g) - g • ModuleCat.freeMk f - f • ModuleCat.freeMk g) ∧ (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (h : A.obj U), r.app U (ModuleCat.freeMk (Sum.inr (Sum.inr h))) = ModuleCat.freeMk (φ.app U h)) ∧ (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (b : B.obj U), p.app U (ModuleCat.freeMk b) = (derivation' φ).d b) ∧ (∃ h : r ≫ p = 0, Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ p h))) ∧ (∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, ∃ h : r.app U ≫ p.app U = 0, Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ (p.app U) h))) ∧ (∃ h : (associatedModules J B).map r ≫ (associatedModules J B).map p = 0, Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ ((associatedModules J B).map p) h))) ∧ (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (b : B.obj U), ((associatedModules J B).map p).val.app U ((CategoryTheory.toSheafify J (symbols B).presheaf).app U (ModuleCat.freeMk b)) = (CategoryTheory.toSheafify J (relativeDifferentials' φ).presheaf).app U ((derivation' φ).d b))
